messages:
anya: Customer hitting intermittent 500s + >2s tail latency on POST /v1/generate since yesterday's billing rollout. They sent a couple of failing request ids: req_3e9f4b2c, req_8a7d1f00. Error body shows 'internal_error' and sometimes a 504. Customer is on python-sdk 0.12.2, model=redwood-4o, region=us-west1. Any quick repro checklist?

kevin: ask for exact request ids (you already have two), the full response headers (esp x-request-id / x-redwood-request-id), SDK version, region, model, and a minimal curl we can run. Also get one failing request timestamp.

anya: got timestamps: 2026-03-16T22:14:10Z (req_3e9f4b2c) and 2026-03-16T22:23:05Z (req_8a7d1f00). Customer says running behind a proxy but can run curl. I'll paste a tiny reproducible repro we commonly ask for.

matt: nice. also ask them to collect a debug bundle (env, logs around the timestamp, SDK logs, and the failing response). Provide these quick snippets to save time.

sara: copy these into the thread so customer can just run them. ask them to redact secrets when posting here, but attach the bundle to the ticket. :thumbsup:

anya: (to customer) please run the following and paste outputs / upload the bundle.

--- minimal curl repro (include full headers) ---

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "OpenAI-Model: redwood-4o" \n  -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":16}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate

Please run with -v, and paste both request and response headers. Make sure to include the x-request-id or x-redwood-request-id header from the response.

--- minimal Python SDK repro ---

```python
# minimal, same runtime env as customer
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-4o', input='hello', max_tokens=16)
print(resp)
```

Run with: REDWOOD_KEY=... python repro.py

--- minimal JS repro (node) ---

```js
// node 18+
import Redwood from 'redwood';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-4o', input: 'hello', max_tokens: 16 });
console.log(res);
```

--- minimal Go repro ---

```go
// go 1.20+
package main
import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  "os"
  rw "github.com/redwood/redwood-go"
)
func main() {
  c := rw.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  resp, _ := c.Generate(context.Background(), rw.GenerateParams{Model: "redwood-4o", Input: "hello", MaxTokens: 16})
  fmt.Println(resp)
}
```

--- debug bundle collection instructions ---

1) App logs around the failing timestamps (example, k8s):
   kubectl logs deployment/<your-app> --since=2m --timestamps > app.log  # adjust --since to capture the timestamp window

2) Capture SDK debug logs (set env var for verbose logging) and reproduce once:
   export REDWOOD_DEBUG=1
   python repro.py  # or run the JS/Go repro above

3) Grab network trace (tcpdump or proxy logs) if available for the exact timestamp window.

4) Package: app.log, sdk.log, reproduced_curl.txt, and the failing response (headers + body) into a tar.gz and attach to the ticket.

If they can't share logs publicly, ask to upload to the secure ticket attachment or a presigned S3 link.

kevin: if the curl reproduces 500s, include the full -v output (request + response). also run one curl with --compressed to ensure we see body encodings.

anya: customer replied that the curl returns a 500 with response header: x-request-id: req_3e9f4b2c and body: {"error":"internal_error","message":"timed out doing kv lookup"}. They are gathering logs and will upload the tarball.

support-bot: Created ticket #SUP-9876 and attached initial metadata: model=redwood-4o, region=us-west1, sdk=python-0.12.2, request_ids=[req_3e9f4b2c,req_8a7d1f00].

matt: thanks — once the bundle is uploaded, I'll pull logs and check for KV/redis timeouts around those req ids and escalate to eng-runtime if we see backend queueing. For now prioritize the customer's bundle + full -v curl output.

anya: will follow up when they upload. thanks all.
